subject: Post-call: VPC connectivity + SDK integration next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finpay.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@finpay.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: VPC connectivity + SDK integration next steps

Hi Alex and Priya — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of discussion:
- FinPay will integrate Redwood for customer-facing LLM features (embedding search + reranker + structured tool calling).
- Primary requirement: private connectivity from FinPay VPC to Redwood (no public egress), strict IP allowlist for control plane calls, and mTLS for additional mutual auth on private endpoints.
- SDK/auth: you plan to use Redwood SDK in service layer behind an internal EGW; will need guidance for API key handling and KMS integration.

Action items / next steps:
1) Lauren (me) — send VPC integration checklist and high-level network diagram (attached).
2) Jonas (cc) — schedule a technical deep-dive to walk through firewall rules, mTLS cert exchange, and DNS/resolution behavior.
3) FinPay — confirm whether you prefer IP allowlist (static egress) or Private Service Connect / PrivateLink style connectivity; share NetOps contact and desired maintenance window for testing.
4) Marissa — will follow up on SOC2 artifacts and onboarding playbook for procurement.

Attachments: redwood_vpc_integration_checklist.pdf, networking-diagram.png (high-level).

Availability: Jonas and I can do a 60-min deep-dive tomorrow or Monday (PST). What times work for your network team?

Thanks again — excited to move forward.

—
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

I’ve looped in our NetOps alias (netops@finpay.com) — they prefer a deep-dive on Monday morning PST. Attached is a contact card for our NetOps lead and a brief network topology we discussed.

Thanks Priya — great, Monday 9–11am PST works for us. 

Quick answers to the items you flagged (so NetOps has something to review before the deep-dive):

1) Connectivity options (high-level)
- IP allowlist + egress: For hosted Redwood API customers we provide documented egress IP ranges per region that you can add to your firewall. These ranges are stable for monthly windows and we publish updates in advance.
- Private endpoint (PrivateLink / Private Service Connect): We also support private endpoints for customers on Dedicated/Private plans — this gives direct VPC-to-VPC connectivity (no public egress) and is recommended for stricter networks.

2) mTLS and DNS
- We support mTLS on private endpoints; mutual authentication is performed using client certs we exchange ahead of provisioning. For PrivateLink-style endpoints DNS is typically resolved by your VPC to the private interface; we’ll provide guidance on split-horizon DNS if needed.

3) SDK and auth
- SDK: standard API key auth is used for control-plane calls. For Private deployments you can plug in customer-managed KMS (we support AWS KMS and GCP KMS) for secret storage. We recommend rotating API keys on a 90-day cadence and can provide a sample rotation script.
- Structured output / tool calling & embeddings: these are handled over the same private connection; embedding vectors are sent over the private link and reranking can happen either on Redwood or locally depending on your preference (we can walk through trade-offs in the tech call).

4) What we’ll bring to the deep-dive
- Jonas will walk through firewall/port requirements, example CIDRs, mTLS cert exchange process, and DNS behavior.
- I’ll bring the procurement checklist and onboarding timeline so we can align procurement + NetOps windows.

Attached: redwood_vpc_integration_checklist.pdf, networking-diagram.png

If you can share an initial firewall rule set (egress ports allowed and current NAT IP ranges) before Monday, Jonas can prepare targeted guidance.

Thanks — looking forward to Monday.

—
Lauren
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: VPC connectivity + SDK integration next steps — technical notes

Hi Priya/Alex — looping in a few technical specifics ahead of the Monday deep-dive so your NetOps folks have something to look at: 

Firewall / Port guidance (example):
- Outbound TCP 443 to Redwood service endpoints (TLS).
- mTLS: TCP 443 as well — will be mutually authenticated using client certs (we do not require additional ports).
- Optional telemetry/paging: outbound TCP 5222 (if you plan to allow X) — we can avoid this if needed.

Sample egress ranges (example only — we will provide official ranges per-region in the tech call):
- us-west-2: 34.72.128.0/24
- us-east-1: 35.190.200.0/24
Please treat these as placeholders; do not use in production until we provide the official published ranges.

mTLS cert exchange (high-level):
1) FinPay generates a CSR and shares the public cert (PEM) via our secure intake link.
2) Redwood signs and returns the client cert (or we accept your internally signed cert if you prefer).
3) We provision the cert to the private endpoint and validate CN/SAN during handshake.
4) Our SDK supports presenting a client cert via the system TLS stack or via an env var pointing to the cert/key pair. We’ll include a sample snippet for Node/Python.

DNS and split-horizon notes:
- For PrivateLink-style endpoints, we recommend a private hosted zone that resolves the Redwood API hostnames to the endpoint IPs. If you have existing wildcard rules, we’ll coordinate to avoid accidental public resolution.

Next steps for Monday deep-dive:
- NetOps to share current NAT egress IPs and firewall ACLs (CSV or snippet).
- We’ll provide an initial test plan: create a small staging service in your VPC, allow the placeholder CIDR, and perform handshake + basic API calls (embeddings + a small generation).

I’ve attached the networking diagram we’ll reference. If you want, I can also include a minimal Terraform snippet to provision a test endpoint and firewall rules.

Thanks — see you Monday.

Jonas Weber
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
